verdict: Revenue surged 29% — Howmet's fastest growth on record — as commercial aerospace and gas turbines pulled hard, and profit grew even faster.

segments.name: Engine Products
segments.note: Turbine blades and other engine parts for aircraft and industrial gas turbines — the biggest and most profitable business, at a 39.1% adjusted EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Fastening Systems
segments.note: Precision fasteners for airframes and engines; growth includes the CAM and Brunner acquisitions (organic growth was 10%).

segments.name: Engineered Structures
segments.note: Large structural airframe parts; sales dipped only because of the Savannah forging-facility divestiture — excluding it, sales rose 8%.

segments.name: Forged Wheels
segments.note: Forged aluminum wheels for heavy trucks, lifted by recovering commercial transportation volumes and aluminum cost pass-through.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative spending — the back office and commercial teams.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Research and development for new engine and airframe components.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear-and-tear charges on factories and equipment, plus amortization of intangibles.

opex.name: Restructuring & other charges
opex.note: Restructuring and other charges — just $2M this quarter.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $48M plus $8M of other expense, taken out of profit.

takeaways.title: Fastest growth on record
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 29% — 25% of it organic — led by commercial aerospace (+32%), gas turbines (+45%) and commercial transportation (+28%).

takeaways.title: Engine Products prints money
takeaways.text: Engine Products' adjusted EBITDA margin widened to 39.1% as spares demand and gas-turbine volumes surged; group adjusted EBITDA rose 43% to $879M.

takeaways.title: Cash is going back to holders
takeaways.text: Free cash flow of $562M funded $500M of buybacks in the quarter, the board added $5B to the repurchase program, and the dividend rose 17% to $0.14.

oneTimers: Special items were small: $9M pre-tax ($7M of CAM/Brunner acquisition costs and $2M of restructuring) plus net discrete tax charges — adjusted net income was $584M vs $567M GAAP.
